name: Elip
confidence_why: 2 independent first-hand sources agree (1 agree, 0 refine), none contradicts
catalog_citation: Boyd, Virginia Lee (2015). The phonological systems of the Mbam languages of Cameroon: a phonological and typological study. LOT Dissertation Series 410. Utrecht: LOT. (downloaded from lotpublications.nl/Documents/)
catalog_locator: sec. 2.6.5 Tone, pp. 134-135 (Elip phonological overview = sec. 2.6, pp. 116-135)
catalog_quote: Elip has a two-tone system underlyingly, high and low. Rising tones and falling tones occur only due to glide formation from syllable mergers. There is a slight lengthening of the vowel due to glide formation in Elip. In addition, tone melodies undergo a loss of contrast in utterance-final position in connection with vowel devoicing or elision. ... High and low tone contrast in monomorphemic noun roots. Four tone melodies are attested in CVCV noun roots ... Noun-class prefixes usually have a low tone, although there are a few exceptions. ... Elip verb roots have three underlying tone melodies: L, HL and H. In verb stems with a H melody, the H spreads one syllable to the right, except onto the final vowel or continuous suffix -a. It is assumed that verbal suffixes are underlyingly toneless. ... In addition to providing lexical contrast, tone also has a grammatical function. Among other t…

audit.quote_check: confirmed in the copy we hold
audit.reasoning: The 'tonal' coding rests on the best available description: a 2015 Leiden/LOT phonology dissertation by the field linguist responsible for the Elip data, with a dedicated tone section whose deciding passage is verbatim in the text we hold at the stated section and pages, and whose whole book never posits word stress or accent for any Mbam language. Glottolog lists no reference grammar or later phonology; the one older phonology (Ekambi 1990, 88-pp Yaounde memoire) was downloaded from MPG PuRe and independently describes Nulibie as a two-level tone language with tone distinctive in the word and no accent. Nothing found suggests a stress analysis exists; no reclassification or re-read needed. Remaining unheld items (Prittie 2002 sketch, un-enumerable SIL Cameroon archive items) are low-value for this record.

sources.citation: Ekambi, Aline. 1990. Esquisse phonologique du nulibie (dialecte yambassa). Memoire de Maitrise en Linguistique, Universite de Yaounde, iii+88 pp. Open copy at MPG PuRe item_403553 (hdl:11858/00-001M-0000-0012-800F-2), file visibility PUBLIC 'with permission from Universite de Yaounde I'.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.quote: 'Les tons sont des unites suprasegmentales, prosodiques, ayant ... une fonction distinctive dans le mot. Ainsi, le changement d'un seul ton dans un mot peut donner lieu a un changement de signifiant et de signifie. ... Nous n'avons trouve que deux niveaux de tons relevant du type ... ton ponctuel' (haut, bas); HL and LH contours described as contextual combinations on vowel sequences; a 'ton moyen' treated as a raised L / lowered H variant, not a third toneme. No occurrence of 'accent', 'intensite' or stress anywhere in the (scanned) text layer.
sources.locator: ch. II.1 'Definition et classement des tons', printed p. 32 (PDF p. 37); also ch. I.1 'Inventaire des tons' pp. 9-11 and 'Identification des tonemes' p. 20ff
sources.note: Only other phonology-specific description of Elip (Nulibie dialect) in Glottolog; independent second source for the tonal coding. downloaded now; confirms two-toneme system with no accent.
